commentary:
The global bond rout is the story this morning, and oil is pouring fuel on it. The US 10-year yield hit 5.33%, its highest since 2002, and the UK 30-year gilt yield broke 6% for the first time since 1998, as stubborn inflation and "higher for longer" warnings — reinforced by Kashkari saying inflation is "still too high" even after a softer PCE print — reset rate expectations across the complex. December Brent punched through $100 (+1.8% to $100.47), WTI added 1.1% to above $92, and product cracks jumped, hardening the inflation feedback loop that's driving yields.

Treasury and Bund futures are stabilising modestly this morning, but gilts remain the weak link (Long Gilt -0.06% vs Bund +0.26%), and the FTSE is down over 1% with euro-area banks off 1.5%. Notably, US index futures are shrugging it off — Nasdaq +0.7% on an upbeat semiconductor outlook and fresh mega-scale AI chip deals, including Tencent's reported Oracle lease. The transmission is classic late-cycle: the dollar is bid against everything, with the euro at a 17-month low on the rates-and-inflation cocktail and French fiscal strain, the yen off 0.6%, and EM FX under pressure.

That dollar-plus-oil combination is squeezing industrial metals — copper -0.7%, iron ore -1.1% — while gold and silver catch an inflation-hedge bid, silver up 1%. In ags, cocoa's 4% slide and robusta weakness lead the softs lower, while KC wheat and sugar firm. Watch jobless claims, Fed speak, and whether Brent holds $100 — a sustained break keeps the pressure on the short end and the curve.
